To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the competitive ratio of any deterministic algorithm is at least 1.5, even when the number of bidders is one and there are no budget constraints; (2) a natural greedy algorithm is optimal when the budget of each bidder is 1; (3) when the number of keywords and bidders is large, a simple randomized algorithm achieves a competitive ratio that is within a small constant factor of optimal.
(1) The competitive ratio of the optimal on-line algorithm is 1/3; (2) The optimal competitive ratio for the problem is 1/2, and (3) The competitive ratio for the optimal on-line strategy is 1/4.

(i) the problem is hard to approximate within a factor of n^1/3 - 1, where n is the number of bidders; (ii) the problem is easy to approximate with an approximation ratio of 2 - 2/(n-1), and (iii) there exists an algorithm whose performance is between the above two bounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following question: what is the competitive ratio of a simple online algorithm for the problem of assigning a sequence of bids (or equivalently a sequence of keywords) to a set of budgeted bidders?
the following question: what is the maximum competitive ratio achievable when selling search keywords on-line, under the constraint that the daily budget of a bidder cannot be exceeded?
the design of an algorithm which, given an input sequence of bids, will assign keywords in a manner that maximizes the expected revenue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the problem of keyword matching with budget constraints is hard to solve.

the competitive ratio of the proposed online algorithm for the problem of keyword matching with budget constrained bidders is 0.5, which is the best possible competitive ratio for this class of problems.
, for the case when there is no budget, and the sequence of bids is known in advance, the competitive ratio is 1/2.
